question: Do nonzero-state event excess and 1-29-sample adjacent-interval burden concentrate where the state-specific remap lacks exact source support?

scope.pair_rule: adjacent events within unit and the same original contiguous rounded-state segment; form pairs before support categorization

support_attribution.primary_position_proxy: nearest physical target depth row to saved Kilosort spike_positions[:,1]; exact ties are ambiguous; row support is exact-coordinate source availability at that rounded state
support_attribution.position_semantics: Kilosort 4.0.27 feature-mass-weighted coordinate over nearby channels, not an observed waveform origin or biological depth
support_attribution.switch_distance_interval_rule: left-closed, right-open; pair bin uses the nearer endpoint; states without a support switch are no_switch

template_proxy.active_channel_threshold: at least 20 percent of the unit maximum channel peak-to-peak
template_proxy.caveat: saved templates are arm-specific refitted Kilosort representations, not state-specific observed waveforms

decision_rule.concentration_evidence: candidate-minus-REF nonzero numerator excess is predominantly in unsupported or mixed position-proxy pairs and this direction agrees with the template-footprint proxy
decision_rule.against_concentration: most positive numerator excess remains in both-supported position-proxy pairs or the two proxies materially disagree
decision_rule.interpretation_limit: association with missing support can prioritize an engineering intervention; it cannot prove duplicate spikes, biological identity, or causality
